name: C#
summary: Statically typed, garbage-collected object-oriented language for the .NET Common Language Infrastructure, standardised as ECMA-334. Known for properties, delegates and events, reified generics, LINQ query expressions, async/await, value types (structs), pattern matching and nullable reference types.

level_notes.0: Roslyn (dotnet/roslyn) is the compiler; execution is by the .NET runtime (dotnet/runtime: CoreCLR with the RyuJIT compiler and GC, Mono, NativeAOT) whose System.Private.CoreLib implements the built-in types. Mono's older mcs compiler is an independent implementation. Both main repositories are too large to list here, so links target individual files on main.
level_notes.1: ECMA-334 (7th edition, 2023 = C# 7) is the ratified standard; the specification published on learn.microsoft.com is the working draft from dotnet/csharpstandard and is ahead of it. Features newer than the draft are defined by the dotnet/csharplang proposals ('feature specifications'). The run-time semantics rest on ECMA-335 (CLI), which is only published as PDF. The keyword/operator/type pages of the Microsoft C# language reference are filed at level 1 as reference manual.
level_notes.2: Microsoft's 'Tour of C#', 'Fundamentals' and 'Programming guide' material is tutorial/guide content and is filed at level 2.
